why: The gallery's label `use` trigger moved onto the hearth stone, where the `strike` trigger already hangs: two `minecraft:interaction` boxes on one cell are coincident, the entity-pick ray enters both at the same distance, and the client resolves the tie by iteration order — so neither is clickable and which one is not decidable from the campaign at all. (The probe used to put the trigger on the case's pedestal beside the `interact` objective; since spec-0093 §6.5 that objective's stone button is the body and no hitbox stands there, so the pair that still contests is two click triggers.) It declares no unit: a click trigger is perfectly writable and the domain binds both kinds; what the engine refuses is holding two at one anchor. What makes it worth committing is what the engine did with the shape before this refusal existed. It exited 0, with `DW0359`, `DW0422` and `DW0489` all green about it — each of those needs one side of its pair to be something else (a standing body, a compiler-owned press set, a cast-ledger NPC), so affordance-against-affordance was nobody's rule. The bot found it instead: `validation/bot-run.sh` over the gallery failed at step 2, before any combat, saying the crosshair could acquire neither box.
